# Build UI in the Interlace craft

Interlace is a shadcn registry (https://ds.interlace.tools) of React components on Base UI and
Tailwind CSS v4. Components are copied into your tree, and every one publishes its contract.
This skill is the other half: how the pieces are meant to be put together, so that a page an
agent writes looks and behaves like one a careful person made.

Use it with the three catalogue skills at
https://ds.interlace.tools/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json: find a component by what it must
do, read its contract, install it. This skill says how to compose and brand what you installed.

## The stance

Seven commitments. Every rule below follows from one of them.

| Commitment | What it means on the page |
| --- | --- |
| Content first | The server HTML holds the whole page, fully visible. Scripts and motion only add to it. |
| Tokens, not values | Every colour, size, gap, radius, duration and easing comes from a CSS variable a brand can retune. |
| One accent | Neutral surfaces; the brand colour marks the one thing that matters in a view. |
| Motion is earned | It explains a change, a direction or an arrival. It never decorates and never blocks reading. |
| Accessible by construction | Measured contrast (AA floor, AAA aim for text), a visible focus ring, keyboard paths, RTL. |
| Composition over overrides | Props, variants and compound parts cover the real cases. Reaching for a class is a signal the component missed one. |
| Brand-neutral | Interlace ships no product's name, copy, colours or scripts. A consumer's brand arrives through tokens and props. |

The bar is the best product teams (Linear, Vercel, Stripe, Apple, Anthropic, Radix, shadcn,
Magic UI, Untitled UI). They are inspiration for the level of care, never a look to copy.

## Set up

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/interlace-base.json   # additive baseline
npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/theme.json            # optional: the Interlace look
npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/button.json           # any component
```

`interlace-base` adds motion tokens, the type scale, container widths, the `xs` breakpoint, radius
steps derived from `--radius`, the colour layers and `color-scheme`. It changes nothing the host
app already styles. `theme` is optional: components work with the host app's own shadcn theme.

## Brand it with tokens

The contract is the shadcn cssVar names. A brand is a set of values for them, declared unlayered
on `:root` and `.dark` in the app's global stylesheet, after the imports:

```css
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.45 0.16 255);          /* the one accent */
  --primary-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);
  --background: oklch(0.985 0.006 85);      /* the page */
  --foreground: oklch(0.18 0.01 85);
  --card: oklch(1 0 0);                      /* sheets lift off the page */
  --muted-foreground: oklch(0.42 0.015 85); /* still AAA on --background */
  --radius: 0.75rem;                         /* every rounded-* follows */
  --highlight: oklch(0.88 0.15 92);          /* optional second voice: one hero action */
}
.dark { /* every token again, for the dark scheme */ }

@theme {
  --font-sans: "Your Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-serif: "Your Serif", ui-serif, Georgia, serif;
  --font-heading: var(--font-serif);         /* the editorial switch, see below */
}
```

Rules of the contract:

- A brand sets values. It does not restyle components, add selectors inside them, or fork a file.
- Light and dark are one axis (`.dark` or `[data-scheme='dark']`); which brand is a second axis
  (`[data-theme='name']`). Every token a theme sets, it sets for both schemes.
- Motion and rhythm retune the same way: `--duration-*`, `--ease-*` and `--spacing-section-*` are
  variables too.
- Every text pair is measured, not eyeballed. The floor, which the theme contract test enforces
  for Interlace's own themes, is WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text, icons, control
  borders (`--input`) and the focus ring (`--ring`). The aim for body text is 7:1 (AAA), which
  the default palette reaches in both schemes.
- More contrast (below) overrides your unlayered values on purpose, so a reader who asks for it
  always gets it. To keep your accent there, set `--contrast-primary` and
  `--contrast-primary-foreground` to a pair you measured at 7:1, and check the tinted surfaces
  built from it too (`text-primary` on `bg-primary/10`).
- The full token list is at https://ds.interlace.tools/semantics-catalog, and writing a full
  theme is at https://ds.interlace.tools/theme-authoring.

## The editorial look

The calm, research-paper register (warm paper, serif headlines, quiet chrome, sources as
footnotes) is a recipe on the tokens above, not a separate kit:

| Ingredient | How |
| --- | --- |
| Paper, not screen white | `--background` a warm off-white; `--card` and `--popover` white, so a card lifts like a sheet |
| Serif headlines, sans body | `--font-heading: var(--font-serif)`. Every Typography heading, CardTitle and pattern title follows. |
| One calm accent | `--primary` only on links, the primary action and the selected state |
| Long reading | `ReadingLayout` (text column plus a table of contents rail), `Typography variant="long"`, `Prose` |
| Receipts | `Citation` on the sentence that makes a claim; `Figure` for a captioned image or chart; `ArticleCard` for the index |
| Quiet bands | `Section` with `tone="muted"` and a `divider` instead of shadows and gradients |

Interlace is packaging this recipe as a `paper` theme and an opt-in editorial voice
(`data-voice="editorial"`: serif headings, softer heading tracking, roomier sections). Once those
are in the registry, use them instead of setting the pieces by hand.

Borders and spacing carry hierarchy; shadows stay small. Illustrations are line drawings in the
foreground or accent colour, never stock imagery.

## Layout and rhythm

- Width comes from `Container` with one of four sizes: `prose` (65ch), `content` (1024px),
  `wide` (1280px), `full`. They map to `max-w-prose`, `max-w-content`, `max-w-wide`.
- A page is a stack of `Section` bands. `spacing` is `tight`, `comfortable` (default) or
  `spacious`, each a fluid token (`--spacing-section-*`, 48 to 128px) that grows on one curve from
  a phone to a laptop. `tone` is `default`, `muted`, `inset` or `brand`; `divider` and `overlap`
  handle the seams.
- Gaps come from `Stack` and `Grid` (`gap` = `xs` 8, `sm` 16, `md` 24, `lg` 40, `xl` 64,
  `2xl` 96 px). On raw elements the same six steps are `gap-2 / 4 / 6 / 10 / 16 / 24`.
- `SectionHeader` opens a band: `eyebrow`, `title`, `tagline`, `align` (`center` or `start`),
  `size` (`default` or `display`). It renders an h2; the page's one h1 belongs to the hero.

## Type

- `Typography` renders every row of the scale with one `variant`: `h1`-`h6`, `body`, `long`,
  `ui`, `ui-sm`, `caption`, `code`; `tone` is `default`, `muted`, `primary`, `destructive`; `as`
  fixes the outline without changing the look (`variant="h2" as="h3"`).
- Display end is fluid: `text-display` (44 to 64px), `text-h1` (40 to 56), `text-section`
  (28 to 40), `text-h2`, `text-h3`. Body stays fixed at 16px (17px for long reads), because text
  that resizes while you read it is harder to read.
- Measure: 65 to 75 characters for any paragraph. Line height 1.6 to 1.7 for body.
- Hierarchy is size, then weight (400, 500, 600, 700). Headlines use `text-balance`.
- Copy is plain and specific: what it does, in the reader's words. No hype, no exclamation marks,
  no emoji as decoration, no fake urgency. A number beats an adjective, and a source beats both.

## Responsiveness

- Mobile first. Base classes describe the narrowest screen; breakpoints add room, never take it
  away. The ladder is Tailwind's (`sm` 640, `md` 768, `lg` 1024, `xl` 1280, `2xl` 1536) plus
  `xs` at 480, all in rem so zoom moves them.
- Collections size to their container, not the viewport. FeatureGrid, StatGroup,
  ArticleListGrid, PricingTable, Testimonial, RelatedPosts and Timeline query their own width
  (`@container`), so the same grid works in a sidebar, a card or a full page. A new collection
  does the same: `@container` on the root, `@md:` and `@4xl:` on the tracks.
- Page chrome (navigation, Container padding, Section rhythm) stays on the viewport ladder.
- Each component declares `MIN_VIEWPORT` (320, 480 or 768). Below it the layout should swap to
  a narrower alternative instead of squeezing the component.
- Touch targets are at least 24 by 24 px (44 for primary actions on phones). Nothing scrolls
  sideways at 320px.
- Check every page at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1440 and 1920 wide, in both schemes.

## Motion

Motion explains what changed and where it went. Three questions before adding any: does it show
a change of state; is the page harder to understand without it; does it leave the layout still?
If any answer is no, leave it out.

| Token | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--duration-fast` | 100ms | Hover, focus, press |
| `--duration-base` | 150ms | Small state changes, overlay enter |
| `--duration-medium` | 250ms | Sheets, larger surfaces |
| `--duration-slow` | 400ms | Continuity between views |
| `--ease-enter` | `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` | Anything appearing (`ease-enter`) |
| `--ease-exit` | `cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.75, 0)` | Anything leaving (`ease-exit`) |
| `--ease-move` | `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)` | Moving between two resting places (`ease-move`) |

Written as `duration-(--duration-fast) ease-enter`, so a brand can retune all of it on `:root`.

The budget:

- Entry animations take 200ms or less and have no delay; first paint belongs to content.
  A stagger spends 150ms in total across all items, not per item.
- Popups (dialog, popover, menu, tooltip) enter from opacity 0 with a slight scale, driven by
  Base UI's `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style`, so exit animates as well as entry.
- Animate `transform`, `opacity` and `filter` only. Height to `auto` is done with
  `grid-template-rows: 0fr` to `1fr`. Layout shift stays at zero: reserve space for anything that
  loads (`aspect-*`, `min-h-*`, the component's own `loading` state).
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the reader sees the end state at once. CSS motion goes
  behind `motion-safe:`; JS motion reads `useReducedMotion()` and skips the animation, not the
  content. A drawn line or a counted number lands at its final state rather than vanishing.
- Off the table: parallax tied to scroll, auto-advancing carousels, cursor-following glows,
  infinite loops on content, and adding another animation library.

The effects tier is a set of finished, tested motion pieces. Each one keeps its content in the
server HTML, hides decoration from assistive tech, and does nothing under reduced motion. Pick by
intent, and spend them: at most one ambient backdrop and one headline effect per view.

| Intent | Reach for |
| --- | --- |
| A block that should be noticed arriving | `Reveal` (`effect` = `fade`, `rise`, `blur`, `scale`) |
| One headline line with a moment of attention | `SplitText` (`by` = `word` or `letter`) |
| A list whose order matters | `StaggerList` |
| One key number | `CountUp` |
| One word that changes in a headline | `RotatingText` |
| The one action or card a page most wants pressed | `Sheen`, `EdgeGlow`, `SheenText` |
| A row of logos or quotes | `Scroller` (has a pause control) |
| A quiet backdrop behind a hero or band | `GridField`, `GradientMesh`, `LightBeam`, `SkyBackdrop`, `Starfield` |
| A question that turns into its answer | `FlipCard`, `GuessReveal` |

Interlace's own brand gestures (`ThreadLines`, `WeaveTexture`, `HeroStrand`, `InterlaceWeave`,
`DecodeText`, `ThreadMark`) express the Interlace identity. On another brand's site, choose from
the neutral rows above.

## Accessibility

- WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor and AAA the aim for text (see the contrast rules above). Colour is never the only signal; pair it with text, an icon or shape.
- Every interactive element shows the focus ring (2px `--ring`, 2px offset). For a custom
  clickable surface, wrap it in `FocusRing`. The ring sits outside the element and never covers
  its text; give scrolling or clipping containers room (`p-1 -m-1`) so it is not cut off.
- More contrast is an AAA reading mode on every theme. It turns on from the system preference
  (`prefers-contrast: more`) or from `data-contrast="more"` on `<html>`; `data-contrast="normal"`
  opts a page out of the system path. The page-set mode also draws focus as a 3px outline.
- `data-density="comfortable"` on `<html>` or a region gives touch-sized controls (44px default,
  `--spacing-control`) and 44px hit areas for small targets.
- Keyboard behaviour comes from Base UI. Composites (menus, tabs, comboboxes, dialogs) are built
  on the existing primitives, never on hand-rolled focus traps or roving tabindex.
- Icons are lucide-react, outlined, sized to the text (`size-4`, `size-5`, `size-6`), and always
  paired with a label or `aria-label`.
- Landmarks and a `SkipLink` on every page; one h1; headings in order.
- RTL works because direction is logical: `ms-*`, `me-*`, `ps-*`, `pe-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`,
  `text-start`, `text-end`, and `rtl:` only for mirrored icons. Dates, numbers and plurals go
  through the Intl APIs. Test every new layout with `dir="rtl"` and a long translation.

## Components: compose, do not override

- Reach for a prop first: `variant`, `size`, `tone`, `align`, `loading`, `disabled`. Button
  variants are `default`, `highlight`, `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`, `link`, `destructive`;
  sizes are `xs`, `sm`, `default`, `lg` and the `icon` set.
- Then composition: compound parts (`Card`, `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardContent`) and the
  Base UI `render` prop to change the element (`<Button render={<Link href="/start" />}>`).
- `className` is accepted for shadcn interop, but needing it means the component missed a case.
  In Interlace itself, add the prop. In an app, keep it to layout placement, and raise the gap.
- Absence is a state, not a null check: use the component's state union and its `loading`
  skeleton, and give every empty, loading and error case real words.
- Every part carries `data-slot`, so tests and analytics select by slot, not by class.
- A flow (phases an app adopts whole: a live room, a booking, a sign-in) has one name per
  part: a namespace for client-only flows (`LiveRoom.Lobby`), flat parts for flows a server
  component can compose (`MultiStepFormStep`). Keep its state in your app, pass it in, and
  handle every event it sends; its file's `## Flow` map lists each phase and the part.
- Server components by default; `"use client"` only where there is state or a browser API.

## Do and don't

```tsx
// Do: tokens, primitives, one accent, a source behind the claim
<Section spacing="comfortable" tone="muted" divider="top">
  <SectionHeader eyebrow="Method" title="How we check a claim" align="start" />
  <Grid cols={3} gap="md">…</Grid>
  <Typography variant="long">
    <Citation sources={sources}>Most readers check one source or none.</Citation>
  </Typography>
</Section>

// Don't: raw values, ad-hoc widths, a second accent, a viewport-keyed grid
<div className="mx-auto max-w-5xl px-[18px] py-20 bg-[#f5f0e8]">
  <h2 className="text-[34px] font-black text-purple-600">How we check a claim</h2>
  <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-[22px]">…</div>
</div>
```

```tsx
// Do: motion that respects the reader and leaves the content in the HTML
<Reveal effect="rise"><Figure … /></Reveal>
<a href="/method" className="transition-colors duration-(--duration-fast) ease-enter hover:text-primary">Method</a>

// Don't: long entry fades, per-item delays, animation that ignores the OS setting
<motion.div initial={{ opacity: 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} transition={{ duration: 0.8, delay: i * 0.2 }} />
```

## Review checklist

- [ ] No raw colour, pixel size or duration in the diff; every value is a token or a scale step.
- [ ] One accent per view; status colours only for status.
- [ ] Width from `Container`, bands from `Section`, gaps from the six steps.
- [ ] Renders at 320px without sideways scroll; collections keyed to their container.
- [ ] Works in light, dark and `dir="rtl"`; contrast measured, not assumed.
- [ ] Keyboard only: every action reachable, focus visible, Escape closes what opened.
- [ ] Reduced motion: same content, no animation; entries 200ms or less; layout shift zero.
- [ ] No product name, copy or colour inside an Interlace component.
- [ ] Copy is plain, specific and sourced.

---

# Interlace Design System — component registry

> 227 installable React components served over the shadcn registry protocol. Every item publishes its contract — the React Server Component boundary, a declared minimum viewport, the keyboard path, the state union it models, and its own semver — so a machine can choose a component on facts instead of on a screenshot.

Install copies source into the consumer tree; there is no runtime package to depend on. MIT. Built on Base UI and Tailwind CSS v4.

## Install

```bash
# any item, by absolute URL — always works
npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/button.json

# the CSS baseline every component assumes (pulled automatically as a
# registry dependency, but install it first for a bare project)
npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/theme.json
```

The `@interlace/<name>` short form also works, but only after the namespace is registered in the consumer's `components.json`. Prefer the absolute URL in generated instructions.

## Craft: how to compose and brand it

Before writing UI with these components, read [https://ds.interlace.tools/.well-known/agent-skills/interlace-craft/SKILL.md](https://ds.interlace.tools/.well-known/agent-skills/interlace-craft/SKILL.md): tokens and theming, the editorial look, layout and fluid rhythm, type, container-query responsiveness, the motion budget and which effect fits which intent, accessibility, and do/don't examples. [https://ds.interlace.tools/llms-full.txt](https://ds.interlace.tools/llms-full.txt) is that guide followed by this file, in one fetch.

To keep it in a repo for Claude Code and other agents that read `.claude/skills/`:

```bash
mkdir -p .claude/skills/interlace-craft
curl -sfL https://ds.interlace.tools/.well-known/agent-skills/interlace-craft/SKILL.md -o .claude/skills/interlace-craft/SKILL.md
```

## Machine-readable index

- [https://ds.interlace.tools/data/agent-index.json](https://ds.interlace.tools/data/agent-index.json): every item with its full contract — tier, rendering boundary, minViewport, keyboard evidence, state unions, ARIA, exports, versions, dependency graph and install command. Start here; it is the only file that lets you FILTER.
- [https://ds.interlace.tools/r/registry.json](https://ds.interlace.tools/r/registry.json): the shadcn registry index (the format the CLI reads).
- [https://ds.interlace.tools/r/{name}.json](https://ds.interlace.tools/r/button.json): one shadcn registry item — full file contents, targets, dependencies.
- [https://ds.interlace.tools/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json](https://ds.interlace.tools/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): what an agent can do here, as skills.
- [https://ds.interlace.tools/data/story-map.json](https://ds.interlace.tools/data/story-map.json): item → Storybook story ids, for a live render of any documented state.
- [https://ds.interlace.tools/data/changelog.json](https://ds.interlace.tools/data/changelog.json): release history, per component.

## How to choose a component

Filter `agent-index.json` on the contract, not on the name. The fields that decide whether an item can be used at all:

- `meta.tier` — Which DS layer the item belongs to: theme, lib, primitive, pattern, template, effects, charts, games. Composition runs upward only — a primitive never imports a pattern.
- `meta.client` — true when the installed file carries the "use client" directive. false means it is safe inside a React Server Component with no boundary.
- `meta.minViewport` — The narrowest viewport in CSS px this component is designed to render correctly at, declared in source as `export const MIN_VIEWPORT`. null means it inherits the min-viewport of whatever it renders and introduces no floor of its own.
- `meta.loading` — true when the component accepts `loading?: boolean` and renders its own skeleton — the DS-wide opt-in, so a caller never hand-rolls a placeholder.
- `meta.version` — The component's own semver, derived from its git history and stamped into the banner of the file you install.
- `meta.since` — The @interlace/ui release the component first shipped in.
- `meta.deprecated` — Present only when the item is on its way out. Carries `removedIn` (a real release, never "eventually") and `replacement`.
- `keyboard` — Observed evidence only. `baseUi` names the Base UI primitive that owns focus and dismissal; `keys` lists the UI Events key values this file branches on itself; `handled` is the disjunction. An item with handled:false is not asserted to be inaccessible — it is asserted to add no keyboard behaviour of its own.
- `states` — The string unions a caller has to satisfy, read from the source. Where a union is a precedence ladder (DATA_STATES) the array order IS the precedence, lowest index wins.
- `a11y` — ARIA roles and attributes written literally in the shipped file, what drives its motion (a CSS driver is clamped by our preflight; a JS driver is out of reach of it), whether the file references prefers-reduced-motion at all, and whether it opts into the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.13 focus ring.

Current distribution across the catalogue:

- rendering: 116 client, 111 server
- keyboard: 176 none, 51 handled
- built-in loading state: 38 of 227
- declared minViewport: 145 at 320, 7 at 480, 1 at 768, 74 at inherited

## Taxonomy

Two axes, both on every item. **Tier** is the DS layer (composition runs upward only). **Category** is intent.

- tier `primitive` — 79 item(s)
- tier `pattern` — 66 item(s)
- tier `effect` — 28 item(s)
- tier `game` — 15 item(s)
- tier `chart` — 14 item(s)
- tier `template` — 13 item(s)
- tier `util` — 6 item(s)
- tier `starter` — 3 item(s)
- tier `theme` — 3 item(s)

- category `primitive` (Primitives) — 79 item(s)
- category `pattern` (Patterns) — 66 item(s)
- category `blog` (Blog & long-form) — 37 item(s)
- category `data` (Data display) — 30 item(s)
- category `effect` (Effects) — 28 item(s)
- category `foundation` (Foundation) — 27 item(s)
- category `form` (Form & input) — 26 item(s)
- category `decorative` (Decorative) — 25 item(s)
- category `navigation` (Navigation) — 18 item(s)
- category `feedback` (Feedback) — 18 item(s)
- category `games` (Games) — 15 item(s)
- category `game` (Games) — 15 item(s)
- category `chart` (Charts) — 14 item(s)
- category `marketing` (Marketing) — 14 item(s)
- category `template` (Templates) — 13 item(s)
- category `overlay` (Overlay) — 10 item(s)
- category `util` (Utilities) — 6 item(s)
- category `a11y` (A11y) — 5 item(s)
- category `starter` (Starters) — 3 item(s)
- category `theme` (Theme) — 3 item(s)
- category `other` (Other) — 2 item(s)

## Items — tier `theme`

- [Interlace Base](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/interlace-base): @interlace/ui — the additive CSS baseline every component needs: motion tokens, type scale, container widths, the xs breakpoint, radius derived from --radius, layered brand + semantic colour tokens in OKLCH, and a color-scheme that follows the dark class so native controls match. Changes nothing the host app already styles.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/interlace-base.json`
  - contract: server, v4.11.1
- [Interlace Foundation](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/interlace-foundation): @interlace/ui — opt-in page-level styling: Inter and JetBrains Mono on font-sans / font-mono, the preflight (body colours, WCAG 2.2 focus ring, media reset, scrollbars), and the fumadocs colour bridge. Restyles the host app by design.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/interlace-foundation.json`
  - contract: server, v3.3.0
- [Interlace Theme](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/theme): @interlace/ui — the Interlace look as shadcn cssVars: points your --primary, --background, --radius and the rest at Interlace's burnt-orange brand tokens (light + dark, AAA). Opt-in; components work without it.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/theme.json`
  - contract: server, v2.0.0

## Items — tier `primitive`

- [Accordion](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/accordion): A disclosure stack: a column of headers whose panels open and close. Wraps @base-ui/react/accordion — Base UI owns the open state (single or multiple), the keyboard model and every piece of the accordion ARIA.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/accordion.json`
  - contract: client, min 320px, keyboard via Base UI accordion, v2.1.0
- [Alert](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/alert): A bordered in-page message with `role="alert"`, an optional leading icon, a title and a description, in two tones (default and destructive).
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/alert.json`
  - contract: server, v2.0.0
- [Alert Dialog](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/alert-dialog): A modal confirmation dialog for *destructive or otherwise consequential* actions ("Delete project", "Sign out everywhere"). Distinct from `Dialog`: the underlying Base UI primitive disables outside-click and Escape-only dismissal so the user MUST…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/alert-dialog.json`
  - contract: client, min 320px, keyboard via Base UI alert-dialog, v2.1.0
- [Aspect Ratio](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/aspect-ratio): A single block-level wrapper that reserves space by ratio (CSS `aspect-ratio`) and stretches to the parent's width. Use it as the *frame* for media that arrives async — images, video, embeds, charts — so the surrounding layout never shifts…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/aspect-ratio.json`
  - contract: server, min 320px, v1.1.0
- [Avatar](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/avatar): A circular image with a text fallback. Wraps @base-ui/react/avatar: Base UI owns the image load/error state machine that decides when the fallback shows, and we own the surface.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/avatar.json`
  - contract: client, loading state, keyboard via Base UI avatar, v1.2.0
- [Badge](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/badge): A small pill for a status, a count, a label or a tag. Renders a `<span>` by default, or whatever Base UI's `render` prop is given, so the same badge can be an anchor without losing its shape.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/badge.json`
  - contract: server, loading state, keyboard via Base UI use-render, v1.3.0
- [Box](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/box): The lowest-altitude layout primitive: surface + box-model on one element. Mirrors MUI `<Box>` (a polymorphic, unopinionated wrapper) minus the `sx` CSS-in-JS prop — Interlace uses a curated, tokenized cva variant set instead, so it cannot reopen the…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/box.json`
  - contract: server, v2.0.0
- [Breadcrumb](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/breadcrumb): A server-rendered, semantically-tagged trail of ancestor links. The compositional API mirrors the shadcn surface so consumers swap drop-in, and `BreadcrumbLink` keeps a server-safe `asChild` seam (`React.cloneElement`, NOT Base UI `useRender`) so the whole…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/breadcrumb.json`
  - contract: server, min 480px, v2.0.0
- [Button](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/button): The minimal-surface counterpart to [dialog.tsx](./dialog.tsx). Where Dialog exercises compound composition + portal + focus, Button exercises the variant + render-prop polymorphism + native-event passthrough surface.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/button.json`
  - contract: client, loading state, keyboard via Base UI use-render, v3.4.0
- [Button Variants](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/button-variants): The cva variant map that `button.tsx` imports — variant × size class strings and nothing else. Pure CVA: no React, no client APIs, so a server component can style a plain `<a>` with `buttonVariants({ variant, size })`.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/button-variants.json`
  - contract: server, v3.3.0
- [Calendar](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/calendar): One month of days to pick one from: the date grid of a booking page, a date field's popup, a "when" step. Days are plain `YYYY-MM-DD` strings (see `calendar-model`), so the day a reader picks is the day the server stores, in every time zone.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/calendar.json`

  - contract: client, min 320px, loading state, keys ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/End/Enter/Escape/Home/Space, states publish|release|action, v2.0.0
- [Time Slider](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/time-slider): Step a chart through time: a play button, a slider with one stop per frame (a year, a survey wave, a season), and the current frame printed large beside them. Any chart goes inside: the slider owns which frame is showing, and the chart is drawn for that…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/time-slider.json`
  - contract: client, min 320px, keyboard via Base UI direction-provider, v1.0.0

## Items — tier `effect`

- [Celebrate](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/celebrate): Small, one-time moments for something the player earned: a streak that hits a milestone, a perfect round, a right answer. `Celebrate` wraps the thing that earned it and, each time `play` changes, sends a short burst of rays and a ring out from it.…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/celebrate.json`
  - contract: client, states primary|success|highlight, v1.0.0
- [Count Up](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/count-up): A number that counts to its value the first time it scrolls into view: "120 sources", "4.8k readers", "98%". The figure is the content, so the component is built around reading it, not around the motion.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/count-up.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Decode Text](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/decode-text): DecodeText — micro-labels resolve from glyph noise into their text.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/decode-text.json`
  - contract: client, v3.0.0
- [Draw On](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/draw-on): A line drawing that draws itself as it scrolls into view: an illustration, a diagram, an arrow that points at the next thing, a signature. Wrap any inline SVG; every stroked shape inside traces its own line, one after another in document order, and filled…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/draw-on.json`
  - contract: client, states sequence|together, v1.0.0
- [Edge Glow](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/edge-glow): A light that runs around the edge of its parent: the plan you recommend, the card that is live right now. Drop it inside a positioned element:
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/edge-glow.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Flip Group](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/flip-group): Items that glide to their new place when a list is sorted, filtered or reordered, instead of jumping there: a leaderboard that re-ranks, results that narrow as a filter is typed, cards that swap. The motion tells the reader where each item went, which a…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/flip-group.json`
  - contract: client, keyboard via Base UI use-render, v1.0.0
- [Gradient Mesh](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/gradient-mesh): A soft, slowly shifting field of colour for a hero or a feature band. A few large blurred glows, each a theme colour, drift on long loops over a base surface, so the band feels alive without anything a reader has to watch. Content goes in `children` and…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/gradient-mesh.json`
  - contract: client, v2.0.0
- [Grid Field](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/grid-field): Graph-paper lines (or a dot grid) behind a section, with a few cells that slowly light up and fade, like squares being filled in on a worksheet. It says "careful, measured work" without saying anything.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/grid-field.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Hero Strand](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/hero-strand): HeroStrand — the thread at page scale: one strand-a ribbon drawn across a hero section, optionally crossed by the strand-b counter. Completes the four scales of "One thread, every scale" (micro: DecodeText, component: InterlaceWeave, page: TimelineMap…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/hero-strand.json`
  - contract: server, v2.0.0
- [Interlace Weave](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/interlace-weave): InterlaceWeave — the brand gesture as an interaction signature.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/interlace-weave.json`
  - contract: server, v3.0.0
- [Light Beam](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/light-beam): A soft cone of light falling into a dark section from an edge, the way a stage light picks out a speaker. It draws the eye to the headline under it and gives a flat surface depth. It does not move: the light is part of the set, not an event.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/light-beam.json`
  - contract: server, states top-left|top|top-right, v1.0.0
- [Marker](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/marker): A highlighter stroke across the one phrase in a paragraph a reader should not miss. The first time the phrase scrolls into view, the stroke sweeps across it from the start of the line to the end, the way a pen would, and wraps across lines with the text.…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/marker.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Pointer Surface](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/pointer-surface): A surface that answers the pointer: a soft light that follows it across a card, a slight tilt toward it, or both. It is the feel of picking a card up off a table, for a grid of choices a reader is weighing (plans, sessions, topics), not for every box on a…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/pointer-surface.json`
  - contract: client, states light|tilt|both, v1.0.0
- [Presence](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/presence): Content that arrives and leaves instead of popping in and out. `Presence` keeps a block on the page for the moment it takes to leave, so a hint, a result or a "you got it" note fades away rather than vanishing. `Swap` trades one piece of content for the…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/presence.json`
  - contract: client, keyboard via Base UI use-render, states fade|rise|scale|blur, v1.0.0
- [Reveal](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/reveal): Any block that arrives as it scrolls into view: a section heading, a card, a figure, a quote. It fades in and, depending on `effect`, rises a little, comes into focus or grows to size, once. Use it on the few things a reader should notice arriving, not on…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/reveal.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Rotating Text](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/rotating-text): One word in a headline that changes every few seconds ("Build for [teams / founders / students]"). It is a familiar pattern done carefully: the line never jumps, a screen reader hears the sentence once, and the reader can stop it.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/rotating-text.json`
  - contract: client, v2.0.0
- [Scroll Text](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/scroll-text): A statement that the reader brings into focus by scrolling: its words go from the muted text colour to the full one, in reading order, as the paragraph moves up the screen. For one large sentence a page is built around (a mission, a finding, a promise)…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/scroll-text.json`
  - contract: client, states p|h1|h2|h3|blockquote|div, v1.0.0
- [Scroller](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/scroller): A row (or column) of items that glides past on a loop: logos of the organisations you work with, short quotes, headlines. The items are real content, so the component treats them that way first and as motion second.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/scroller.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Sheen](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/sheen): A soft band of light that crosses its parent every few seconds. Drop it inside the one button or card a page most wants pressed:
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/sheen.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Sheen Text](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/sheen-text): A word or short phrase painted with a slow, travelling gradient: the one word of a headline that carries the promise. Use it once per view, on a few words, never on body text.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/sheen-text.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Sky Backdrop](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/sky-backdrop): A calm daytime sky for a friendly hero: a soft gradient, a warm sun glow in one corner, and a few clouds drifting across. It suits pages that want warmth rather than drama, the light counterpart to `Starfield`.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/sky-backdrop.json`
  - contract: client, states top-left|top-right|none, v2.0.0
- [Split Text](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/split-text): A headline or short line that arrives a word, or a letter, at a time the first time it scrolls into view. It gives one line on a page a moment of attention; use it once or twice per page, on text short enough to read while it arrives.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/split-text.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Stagger List](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/stagger-list): A list whose items arrive one after another the first time it scrolls into view: steps of a process, recent updates, the points of an argument. The arrival gives the eye an order to read in; the list itself is ordinary.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/stagger-list.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Starfield](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/starfield): A night sky behind a hero: still stars, a share of them breathing, an occasional shooting star and a few slow meteors. Everything is painted on ONE `<canvas>` driven by ONE animation frame loop, so the whole sky costs a single layer and a single callback…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/starfield.json`
  - contract: client, v2.0.0
- [Thread Lines](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/thread-lines): Interlace's own backdrop: a loose bundle of threads running across a section, crossing and parting the way strands do in a weave, with a small glint of light travelling along each one. It is the brand mark (two strands, interlaced) at the scale of a page.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/thread-lines.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Underline Link](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/underline-link): A text link whose underline draws itself in when the reader points at it or tabs to it, from the start of the line to the end, and wraps across lines with the text. For links in running text, navigation and footers where a hard underline on every link…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/underline-link.json`
  - contract: server, keyboard via Base UI use-render, v1.0.0
- [View Transition](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/view-transition): The browser's View Transitions API, made safe to reach for: a card grows into its detail page, a list reorders in place, and a page change cross-fades instead of blinking. Interlace adds only what the API leaves to every app: a fallback where it is…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/view-transition.json`
  - contract: client, v1.0.0
- [Weave Texture](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/weave-texture): A quiet woven cloth behind a section: warp threads in `--strand-a` and weft threads in `--strand-b`, passing over and under each other in a plain weave. It is texture, not glow: nothing moves, nothing shines, and at the default strength it sits just above…
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/weave-texture.json`
  - contract: server, v1.0.0

## Items — tier `starter`

- [A11y Starter](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/a11y-starter): @interlace/ui — the three a11y primitives + the reduced-motion hook every consumer should install on day one.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/a11y-starter.json`
  - contract: server, v5.2.0
- [Layout Starter](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/layout-starter): @interlace/ui — the six layout primitives that compose every page. One install, the LAYOUT_PHILOSOPHY contract is satisfied.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/layout-starter.json`
  - contract: server, v5.2.0
- [MDX Starter](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/mdx-starter): @interlace/ui — the components most MDX pipelines need (Callout, Prose, CodeBlock, Tag), wired through a default mdx-components.tsx.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/mdx-starter.json`
  - contract: server, v5.2.0

## Items — tier `util`

- [cn — class-name merge utility](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/cn): @interlace/ui — the cn() helper, alias-compatible with shadcn. Merges Tailwind class lists deterministically.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/cn.json`
  - contract: server, v2.1.0
- [No-flash theme bootstrap script](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/theme-script): @interlace/ui — the inline `<head>` script that applies the stored theme before first paint. Without it every page load flashes the default theme.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/theme-script.json`
  - contract: server, states default|lg|xl, v1.0.1
- [Theme token manifest](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/theme-tokens): @interlace/ui — the registry of themes and the list of every `--interlace-*` token a theme must define. A missing token does not throw; it silently inherits the previous theme's value.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/theme-tokens.json`
  - contract: server, states primary|primary-hover|primary-active|primary-foreground|primary-subtle|primary-subtle-foreground|background|foreground|card|card-foreground|popover|popover-foreground|muted|muted-foreground|border|input|ring|accent|accent-foreground|secondary|secondary-foreground|destructive|destructive-foreground|success|success-foreground|warning|warning-foreground|info|info-foreground|caution|caution-foreground|highlight|highlight-foreground|scrim|scrim-foreground|hero-star|hero-trail|hero-meteor|hero-surface|hero-surface-deep|hero-foreground|window-control-close|window-control-minimize|window-control-zoom|strand-a|strand-b|chart-1|chart-2|chart-3|chart-4|chart-5|viz-grid|viz-axis|viz-edge|radius|brand-mark-bar-o|brand-mark-bar-g, v3.1.0
- [useReadingPrefs hook](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/use-reading-prefs): @interlace/ui — reads and writes the reader's text size (`data-text-size`) and contrast (`data-contrast`) on <html>, persists both, and follows `prefers-contrast` when no choice is stored.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/use-reading-prefs.json`
  - contract: client, states more|normal|system, v1.0.0
- [useReducedMotion hook](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/use-reduced-motion): @interlace/ui — the `useReducedMotion` hook every interactive primitive uses to gate animations on the user's OS preference.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/use-reduced-motion.json`
  - contract: client, v3.0.0
- [useTheme hook](https://ds.interlace.tools/c/use-theme): @interlace/ui — reads and writes the theme (`data-theme`) and colour scheme (`.dark`) axes, persists to localStorage, and follows the OS when no preference is stored.
  - install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ds.interlace.tools/r/use-theme.json`
  - contract: client, v1.1.0
